 50,000 Americans getting automatic $5,000 refunds from IRS: Here’s who qualifies
 Published: Oct. 22, 2026, 2:16 p.m. 
 Under a reinterpretation of the Working Families Tax Cut laws by the Treasury Department, people will receive the credit in the form of payments, capped at $5,000 per child. AP Photo/Eric Gay, File 
 Set as Google Preferred Source 
 By Leada Gore | lgore@al.com 
 More than 50,000 Americans will be getting $5,000 refunds related to past tax credits, the U.S. tax agency announced.
 The Internal Revenue Service has begun issuing refunds related to carryforwards from the adoption tax credit. The money, according to 24/7 Wall Street, comes from unused tax credits that families have been carrying forward year after year because their tax bills were too small to absorb them. 
 Under a reinterpretation of the Working Families Tax Cut laws by the Treasury Department, people will receive the credit in the form of payments, capped at $5,000 per child.
 The payments will be issued automatically, and people do not need to submit an amended return.
 “By issuing refunds without requiring eligible families to file an amended return, the IRS is helping reduce the financial burden on those who decided to adopt a child into their family,” IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank Bisignano said. “This administrative change will help families access the tax benefits they are entitled to as quickly and simply as possible.”
 To qualify, you must have carried an unused adoption credit from 2020 through 2024 into 2026 and filed your return before April 15, 2026.
 Prior to the change, any old money carried forward could only offset any taxes that were owed. For lower-income families that didn’t owe taxes, the credit could sit unused for years.
 The IRS said they expect the refunds to be complete by the end of the year. Eligible taxpayers will receive a notice from the IRS within 30 days of the adjustment to let them know the amount and if it was applied to another tax or non-text debt.
